questions.question: Explain why granite has large crystals but basalt has small crystals.
questions.expected_answer: Both are igneous rocks formed from cooling molten rock. Granite formed from magma that cooled slowly deep underground over thousands to millions of years, giving crystals time to grow large; basalt formed from lava that cooled quickly at the surface, so crystals had little time to grow and stayed small.

questions.question: Describe the stages by which a granite mountain could become sandstone.
questions.expected_answer: Weathering by water, ice, temperature changes and plants breaks the granite into fragments; erosion carries the sand grains away by rivers or wind; deposition lays the sand down in layers when the water slows; compaction by overlying layers squeezes the grains together and cementation by minerals such as silica or calcite glues them into sandstone.

questions.question: State the difference between how metamorphic and igneous rocks form, and give two examples of metamorphic rocks with their parent rocks.
questions.expected_answer: Igneous rocks form when molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies; metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are changed by heat and/or pressure without melting. Examples: shale becomes slate; limestone becomes marble; sandstone becomes quartzite; granite becomes gneiss.
